notes: Identity checked independently from supplied document: title Brain Drain: The Mere Presence of One’s Own Smartphone Reduces Available Cognitive Capacity; authors Adrian F. Ward, Kristen Duke, Ayelet Gneezy, Maarten W. Bos; DOI 10.1086/691462; JACR volume 2 number 2, published online April 3, 2017. Supplied canonical text contains the primary journal article, printed pp. 140–154, including experiment methods/results and references; not merely an abstract or a secondary report. No PDF path was supplied, so no PDF rendering was possible or performed. Canonical text OCR uses 5 for equals and h2 for eta squared; quotes retain these literal characters. All three assigned rows identify experiment 2 with the same generic description and PDF p.8 (printed p.147). Neither row order nor requested metric distinguishes the target. Candidate tests on that page: OSpan Phone Location main effect F(2,263)=3.53, p=.03, printed partial eta squared .026; Phone Power main effect F(1,263)=.05, p=.83; Power × Location F(2,263)=1.05, p=.35; planned linear location trend F(1,263)=7.05, p=.008, printed partial eta squared .026; quadratic trend F(1,263)=.001, p=.98; other-room versus desk paired comparison printed Mdiff=4.67, p=.008; pocket/bag versus desk Mdiff=2.30, p=.20; pocket/bag versus other-room Mdiff=2.37, p=.17. The page also gives the pockets versus bags comparison p=.55. No candidate is assigned to a row. Same-test p values and printed metrics are kept together here; no conversions performed. The .026 printed for two distinct tests cannot resolve correspondence. Printed p.146 explicitly gives a final sample of 275 participants after excluding 11 without smartphones, 4 for OSpan accuracy below 85%, and 6 for missing (5) or extreme (1) Go/No-Go response times, from 296 recruits. This is a final-study sample candidate, not an established analytic N for an identified row-specific test. No N is inferred from degrees of freedom and no N sum is extracted. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders; do not overwrite prior verified fields.
